definition: Trigrams are a special case of the n-gram, where n is 3.
details: They are often used in natural language processing for performing statistical analysis of texts and in cryptography for control and use of ciphers and codes. See results of analysis of "Letter Frequencies in the English Language".

explainer.lead: A trigram is an n-gram of length three, used to capture short local patterns in text or symbol streams. It matters because these three-item patterns are a cheap, robust signal for statistics, matching and cipher analysis.

tiers.eli5: Think of reading a sentence three letters or three words at a time, like sliding a window of three across the page and noting every chunk you see.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers index trigrams to speed up fuzzy string search and to build language models that estimate the next token from the previous two; a common pitfall is data sparsity, since many trigrams never appear in training.
tiers.paperLevel: A trigram is a special case of the n-gram with n = 3; in a corpus the probability P(w3 | w1, w2) is estimated by counting occurrences of the three-item sequence, and unreliable estimates arise where counts are low.

explainer.example: From the text 'HELLO', the overlapping character trigrams are 'HEL', 'ELL' and 'LLO'.
